samples.summary: Read-only sheet mounts never recalculate cross-sheet formulas, so a viewer can render stale cached values indefinitely
samples.evidence: `runRemoteSync(!readOnly)` (line 1308) and `scheduleRemoteSync(readOnly ? false : needsRecalc(ops))` (line 1322) hard-code `needsRecalc=false` for a read-only mount, and `Spreadsheet.recalculateCrossSheetFormulas` (packages/sheets/src/view/spreadsheet.ts:973) additionally returns after a bare `render()` when `_readOnly`. The recalc is the only thing that refreshes a formula referencing another tab. The cached value in the CRDT is only refreshed by a client that has the *dependent* tab open and may write; if the only client watching that tab is a share-link viewer, the displayed value never updates after a peer edits the source tab. The tradeoff is documented in the comments, but the observable result is a wrong number on the screen of a real user on a real path, not merely a skipped write.

samples.summary: `assertWritable` throws from async comment mutators whose callers have no catch, turning a refused write into an unhandled rejection rather than a message
samples.evidence: `assertWritable` throws inside `async addThread/addReply/editComment/deleteComment/setThreadResolved`, so the call rejects. `handleCommentEdit` (sheet-view.tsx:967) and `handleCommentDelete` (sheet-view.tsx:974) are `await storeRef.current?.editComment(...)` with no try/catch, and `handleCommentResolve` (sheet-view.tsx:940) likewise. Today the popover is passed `readOnly` and hides those affordances, so the path is unreachable — which is exactly why the throw is described as a last line of defence. If it ever does fire it produces an unhandled promise rejection in a click handler rather than the toast/draft-preserving behaviour the neighbouring handlers were written for.

samples.summary: Proxy `isExtensible` is hard-coded to `true` and `preventExtensions` to `false`, which violates proxy invariants if the wrapped store is ever non-extensible
samples.evidence: `isExtensible: () => true` must agree with `Reflect.isExtensible(target)`; `ownKeys` must return the target's exact own keys when the target is non-extensible, and `getOwnPropertyDescriptor` may not report an existing own property as absent in that case. If any caller (or a future `Object.freeze`/`Object.seal` on `YorkieNoteStore`/`MemNoteStore`) makes the target non-extensible, the `isExtensible`, `ownKeys` and `getOwnPropertyDescriptor` traps all start throwing `TypeError`, and a plain spread or `Object.keys` on the handle crashes the read-only mount. Neither store does this today, so this is a latent hazard rather than a live crash.

samples.summary: Split-pane divider drag ignores the grab offset, so the divider now snaps by up to its own 25px width on the first pointermove
samples.evidence: `const ratio = (ev.clientX - rect.left) / track` treats the pointer position as the divider's *left edge*, but the pointer may be anywhere inside the 25px hit area at pointerdown. The new `track = rect.width - divider.offsetWidth` correctly removes the divider from the denominator, yet the offset between where the user grabbed and the divider's left edge is never captured, so the divider jumps to meet the cursor. The same error existed at 7px (barely visible); widening the divider to 25px makes it a visible snap — the very case the width change was meant to improve.

samples.summary: The 120s DuckDB warm-up shares one 180s `beforeAll` budget with fixture seeding, so a slow download can still time the hook out
samples.evidence: `jest.setTimeout(180_000)` (line 50) is the whole budget for the hook, which first runs `readLakehouseFixtureManifest()` and `leg.seed()` for every storage backend (network round-trips to MinIO/Azurite) and only then `await duckDb.withConnection(async () => undefined, WARMUP_TIMEOUT_MS)` with `WARMUP_TIMEOUT_MS = 120_000`. If seeding takes more than ~60s and the ~170MB extension download runs long, the hook exceeds 180s and the suite fails — the same network-flake failure mode the warm-up was added to remove, merely relocated from the first test to the hook.
